Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

multigrain (development version)

New functionality

  • stopping_rule_gsd() creates an efficacy stopping rule for a group sequential design: one Boolean condition over the rejection indicators r1, r2, ... per interim analysis (or a single condition applied at every interim). Pass it to graph_optimise_gsd() or calc_power_pvals_gsd() through their new stopping_rule argument and each simulated trial stops at the first interim analysis whose condition holds, so the gain and every reported power count only the rejections made before the trial stopped. calc_power_pvals_gsd() also reports stop_distribution, the proportion of trials stopping at each analysis, and mean_stop_look. A trial that rejects every hypothesis stops at that analysis with or without a rule. Stopping only removes rejections, so error control is unaffected.
  • sf_hsd_opt() tags a hypothesis whose Hwang-Shih-DeCani spending parameter is to be chosen by the optimiser rather than fixed in advance. Hypotheses with the same id share a parameter; bounds (default c(-4, 1), within -10 to 2) and step (0.5, 0.25 or 0.125) set the lattice of values searched. Given one or more such entries, transform_pvalues_gsd() returns a multigrain_pvals_gsd_spec object holding the raw p-values and a boundary table for every lattice node, each checked for well ordering when the spec is built, so every value the search can try is a valid transform.
  • resolve_pvalues_gsd() turns a spec and a value per spending parameter into the multigrain_pvals_gsd object transform_pvalues_gsd() would have returned with those values fixed, from the stored tables. Use it to evaluate a fixed choice, to reproduce an optimised result’s final evaluation, or to check a chosen design on fresh simulated p-values.
  • graph_optimise_gsd() accepts a spec and optimises the spending parameters jointly with the graph: a genetic algorithm with one gene per parameter, then a COBYLA refinement of the graph at every lattice node of each parameter, warm-started from its neighbour. The result adds spending_param, hyp_spending_param, spending, spending_bounds, spending_step, spending_group, spending_profile (the gain at each node with the graph re-optimised and with it fixed, and the paired difference from the optimum with its standard error), spending_search and profile_converged; print() shows the spending functions and the range of values within 5e-4 of the best gain, and summary() the profile. A result without optimised spending is unchanged.

Bug fixes

  • graph_optimise_gsd() and calc_power_pvals_gsd() now check that the graph has as many hypotheses as the p-values and abort with a message naming both numbers; previously the mismatch surfaced only as the internal error “G must be an m x m matrix”.
  • graph_optimise() and calc_power_pvals() now refuse a gain function created with trial_success_gsd(), which needs decision times; previously the object was accepted and every rejection was silently scored as an analysis-1 rejection. Use graph_optimise_gsd() and calc_power_pvals_gsd().
